title: Console visual QA: every page at 1440 and 390, light and dark
label: console-qa

steps.prompt: Capture, do not review. In apps/swarm-ui run `npm ci` and start `npm run dev` in the background (the fixture build, no network). When http://localhost:5173 answers, run `python -m swarm_qa capture --routes apps/swarm-ui/qa/routes.json --group overview-automate --base http://localhost:5173 --presets desktop,phone-390 --themes light,dark --out $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/capture-overview-automate --bundle $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/capture-overview-automate.tar`. It writes the tarball whatever happens: a route that failed is listed in its manifest's `failed`, not a reason to stop. If it exits non-zero, put its last 40 lines in your answer and still make sure capture-overview-automate.tar exists under $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR. Change no file in the repository.

Visual QA review of the console's fixture build. Unpack capture-overview-automate.tar. For every PNG its manifest.json lists, open the image with the Read tool and look at it: layout, overflow and clipping, alignment, spacing, truncation, contrast in dark mode, anything that differs between desktop (1440) and phone-390 that should not, and anything that contradicts the page's own text file. Each route its manifest lists as failed is itself a finding. For each finding write a crop PNG named <id>.png showing it, and an entry in findings-overview-automate.json in the shape of docs/design/visual-qa.md section 4.4, with reviewed set to the number of images you opened. Bundle findings-overview-automate.json and the crops into review-overview-automate.tar under $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR. Change no file in the repository.

Goal-driven flow test of the console's fixture build. In apps/swarm-ui run `npm ci` and start `npm run dev` in the background; open http://localhost:5173 in the live browser at the desktop preset. Run `swarm-handoff record start flow-find-failure`. Using the jev browser tools, reach this goal as a person would, without typing addresses: find the most recently failed task and open its logs, then its attempts. Run `swarm-handoff record stop`. Then switch to the phone (`swarm-handoff device phone-390`) and do it again, recorded as flow-find-failure-phone. For each run write in flow-find-failure.json: whether the goal was reached, the steps taken, and every point where a label was missing, ambiguous or misleading, each with a screenshot taken with browser_take_screenshot and no filename (it is saved under $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/screenshots). List in flow-find-failure.json every screenshot you take, by its file name, with what it shows, a finding's or not: the report treats a screenshot no json describes as one you may not have seen. Bundle flow-find-failure.json, flows/flow-find-failure.gif, flows/flow-find-failure-phone.gif and the screenshots into flow-find-failure.tar under $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR. Change no file in the repository.

Goal-driven flow test of the console's fixture build. In apps/swarm-ui run `npm ci` and start `npm run dev` in the background; open http://localhost:5173 in the live browser at the desktop preset. Run `swarm-handoff record start flow-workflow-graph`. Using the jev browser tools, reach this goal as a person would, without typing addresses: open a workflow that has a failed step, find which step failed and why, and open that step's changes. Run `swarm-handoff record stop`. Then switch to dark mode (`swarm-handoff theme dark`) and do it again, recorded as flow-workflow-graph-dark; run `swarm-handoff theme system` when it is done. For each run write in flow-workflow-graph.json: whether the goal was reached, the steps taken, and every point where a label was missing, ambiguous or misleading, each with a screenshot taken with browser_take_screenshot and no filename (it is saved under $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/screenshots). List in flow-workflow-graph.json every screenshot you take, by its file name, with what it shows, a finding's or not: the report treats a screenshot no json describes as one you may not have seen. Bundle flow-workflow-graph.json, flows/flow-workflow-graph.gif, flows/flow-workflow-graph-dark.gif and the screenshots into flow-workflow-graph.tar under $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR. Change no file in the repository.

Scripted flow test of the console's fixture build with the Playwright browser tools. Your budget is 35 minutes, inside this step's 45-minute timeout: run `date +%s` first and keep the start, check the elapsed time before every step, and at 35 minutes stop wherever you are, run `swarm-handoff record stop`, and write and bundle what you reached. In apps/swarm-ui run `npm ci` and start `npm run dev` in the background. When `curl -s -o /dev/null -m 10 http://localhost:5173` answers, open http://localhost:5173 in the live browser with browser_navigate and take a browser_snapshot; start a recording only after that snapshot shows the console, and wait for `swarm-handoff record start` to print its answer before the next browser tool call (the recorder connects to the same browser, and a navigation made while it connects can hang). If a browser tool refuses your own call as malformed (a required argument missing or invalid, such as browser_find with neither text nor regex), the page has not failed: correct the call and retry it once; a second refusal ends the run like a failure. If the page or the browser fails (a timeout, a navigation error, a closed page), or a call returns any other error, do not call it or any other browser tool again, not even to list tabs: run `swarm-handoff record stop`, write the error, the step it stopped at and what you reached, and every screenshot taken so far with what it shows, in flow-submit-form.json with goal_reached false, bundle, and finish. At the desktop preset and then at the phone (`swarm-handoff device phone-390`, then a browser_snapshot), record a flow with `swarm-handoff record start flow-submit-form-<preset>` and `swarm-handoff record stop`: open the task form, `/submit/task` in apps/swarm-ui/qa/routes.json (route `new`), the way a person reaches it: the rail's Submit item, then Start an agent; try to submit it empty, read every validation message, fill each field, choose each runner profile in turn and note what the form shows for it, and stop before the final submit. Take a browser_take_screenshot with no filename at each step, at most 12 screenshots per preset: one for the empty submit, one per runner profile whose form differs from the last, the rest for messages (it comes back to you as an image and is saved under $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR/screenshots). Say in flow-submit-form.json, for each preset, goal_reached and the elapsed minutes. List in flow-submit-form.json every screenshot you take, by its file name, with what it shows, so the report can tell whether you saw the image. Note every message that is missing, wrong or clipped, with its screenshot. Bundle flow-submit-form.json, flows/flow-submit-form-desktop.gif, flows/flow-submit-form-phone-390.gif (each that exists) and the screenshots into flow-submit-form.tar under $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR. Change no file in the repository.

Accessibility pass of the console's fixture build. In apps/swarm-ui run `npm ci` and start `npm run dev` in the background; open http://localhost:5173 in the live browser at the desktop preset. For each top-level section, using only the keyboard (Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Escape, arrows): reach every control, open and close every dialog and inspector, and note where focus is lost, invisible or trapped. Then take browser_snapshot of each page and note controls with no accessible name. Then, through swarm_browser.live(), repeat one page per section with emulate_media(reduced_motion='reduce') and with Emulation.setEmulatedVisionDeficiency set to deuteranopia, and screenshot each. Write a11y-keyboard.json in the findings shape of docs/design/visual-qa.md section 4.4, with a screenshot per finding, and bundle it with the screenshots into a11y-keyboard.tar under $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR. Change no file in the repository.

Write the console visual QA report of the screens. Unpack every staged tar, each into its own directory named after its step (every capture tar carries a manifest.json at its root): the six captures', the six reviews' and the a11y pass's. For each group, count the images its capture's manifest.json lists and check the review's reviewed count against that number; report any shortfall as a finding about the run itself, naming both numbers: a review that looked at nothing is not a clean review. A staged tar that is missing is also a finding about the run itself, naming the tar; when a capture tar is missing, check that group's reviewed count against the images its routes in apps/swarm-ui/qa/routes.json should have produced (two presets, two themes, each route's segments) instead, and say which count you used. Merge every finding into findings.json, de-duplicating the same defect seen at several sizes into one finding that lists each. Write report.md: one line first saying the flows are reported apart, in the flow-report step's flows.md, so that a flow that fails never costs these findings; then a summary table (findings by severity and by page), then each finding, severity first, with its crop PNG embedded by relative link. Write nothing about the flows here. Copy every crop PNG, and every screenshot a finding cites (its source, a full-size capture from its group's capture tar), to $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR next to report.md and findings.json so the console shows them; a cited screenshot that no staged tar holds is a finding about the run itself. Change no file in the repository.

Write the console visual QA report of the flows. Unpack every staged tar: flow-find-failure.tar, flow-workflow-graph.tar and flow-submit-form.tar. Write flows.md: one section per flow, and in it, for each of its runs (preset or theme), the run's GIF embedded by relative link, whether its goal was reached, the steps taken, and each label found missing, ambiguous or misleading beside its screenshot. A run that stopped on its budget or on a browser tool's timeout is reported as stopped, with the step it reached and the error it recorded, never as a goal reached. Then each flow-submit-form screenshot embedded beside what the model said it saw in it; a screenshot in the tar that the flow's json does not describe is a finding about the run, since the model may not have seen it. Write flows.json: per flow and run, goal_reached and its label findings in the findings shape of docs/design/visual-qa.md section 4.4. The screen findings are the report step's report.md and findings.json; do not repeat them. Copy every GIF and every screenshot flows.md embeds to $SWARM_ARTIFACTS_DIR next to flows.md and flows.json so the console shows them. Change no file in the repository.
